questions.q: In the $100 bill story, what does the bill represent?
a: Your worth, however you are treated
A reward for hard work
The cost of mistakes
The value of money over friendship
questions.why: Lesson 1 uses the story to say your worth stays the same however you're treated.

questions.q: What does the teacher do to the $100 bill in the story?
a: Crumples it and stomps on it
Hides it in a book
Gives it to the best student
Tears it into pieces
questions.why: She crumples it, drops it and stomps on it, and its value remains.

questions.q: What does the lesson about the zig and the zag say?
a: You can't keep the good without accepting the bad
Good luck is mostly random
Stability is always achievable
Risk should always be avoided
questions.why: Lesson 2 says you can't remove all risk without removing all rewards.

questions.q: Which example illustrates the zig and zag?
a: A YouTube channel whose views spike and then fall
A gardener whose plants fail in winter
A runner who wins and then retires
A student who passes and fails exams
questions.why: The author uses a YouTube channel's rising and falling views.

questions.q: What belief does lesson 3 want you to hold?
a: No matter what, tomorrow can be a good day
Past struggles predict the future
Good days are rare
Only big wins bring happiness
questions.why: Lesson 3 is the author's epitaph that tomorrow can be good.
